name: Cerro Champaquí
why: Three days across the high grass of the Sierras Grandes to the roof of Córdoba province, sleeping in the stone puestos of the Río Tabaquillo valley.
book: No permit. Villa Alpina is at the end of a long dirt road from Villa General Belgrano. The refuges and puestos in the Río Tabaquillo valley are private family houses: book a bed and meals ahead, or go with a local guide.
water: Streams on the way and at the refuges; treat it. Nothing on the summit ridge.
dangers: Summer storms with lightning and violent gusts build fast in the afternoon.
Fog on the plateau: the paths split and are easy to lose.
Cold below zero in winter; heat, sun and dehydration in summer.
turnaround: Leave the refuge for the summit at dawn and be back off the ridge by 14:00, before the storms.

points.name: Villa Alpina
points.note: A hamlet of chalets in pine woods at about 1,400 m, at the end of the dirt road. The path climbs west onto the open grass of the sierra.

points.name: Río Tabaquillo refuges
points.note: Family-run stone refuges and puestos at about 2,100 m in the Río Tabaquillo valley, 7-8 hours from Villa Alpina. Sleep here both nights.

points.name: Cerro Champaquí summit
points.note: 2,790 m, the highest point of Córdoba, with a small lake below the top that freezes from April to August. Back to the refuges, then down to Villa Alpina.
